# Two-sample t-test sample size calculation
# Design: one-sided test, H0: μ_t = μ_c vs H1: μ_t > μ_c
# Parameters
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.80
delta <- 4.3  # expected difference (dBA)
sigma <- 7.8  # common SD (dBA)
allocation_ratio <- 1  # 1:1 allocation

# Critical value for one-sided test
z_alpha <- qnorm(1 - alpha)

# Non-centrality parameter coefficient
# For two-sample t-test with equal allocation: ncp = delta / (sigma * sqrt(2/n))
# Effect size (Cohen's d)
cohens_d <- delta / sigma
cat("Cohen's d (effect size):", round(cohens_d, 4), "\n")
cat("Z-critical (one-sided, alpha=0.05):", round(z_alpha, 4), "\n\n")

# Search for minimum n per group
# Start with a reasonable guess based on normal approximation
n_approx <- 2 * ((z_alpha + qnorm(target_power)) / cohens_d)^2
cat("Approximate n per group (normal approximation):", round(n_approx, 1), "\n\n")

# Refine with t-distribution
# For one-sided test: df = 2n - 2, critical value = t_{1-alpha, df}
# Non-centrality parameter: lambda = (delta / sigma) * sqrt(n/2)
# Power = P(T > t_{1-alpha, df} | lambda)

# Function to calculate power given n per group
power_calc <- function(n_per_group) {
  if (n_per_group < 1) return(0)
  
  df <- 2 * n_per_group - 2
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df)  # Critical value for one-sided test
  
  # Non-centrality parameter
  # lambda = (difference / sigma) * sqrt(n / 2) for equal sample sizes
  lambda <- (delta / sigma) * sqrt(n_per_group / 2)
  
  # Power: probability that non-central t > critical value
  power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp = lambda)
  
  return(power)
}

# Search for minimum integer n
powers <- numeric(100)
ns <- 1:100

for (i in 1:100) {
  powers[i] <- power_calc(i)
}

# Find minimum n achieving target power
min_n <- which(powers >= target_power)[1]

cat("Sample size search results:\n")
cat("n per group | Power\n")
cat("------------|-------\n")

# Show values around minimum
for (n_test in max(1, min_n - 2):min(min_n + 2, 100)) {
  p <- power_calc(n_test)
  marker <- if (n_test == min_n) " <-- MINIMUM" else ""
  cat(sprintf("%11d | %6.4f%s\n", n_test, p, marker))
}

cat("\n=== RESULT ===\n")
cat("Minimum sample size per group achieving ≥80% power:", min_n, "\n")
cat("Power at minimum n =", min_n, ":", round(power_calc(min_n), 4), "\n")

if (min_n > 1) {
  cat("Power at preceding design (n =", min_n - 1, "):", round(power_calc(min_n - 1), 4), "\n")
}

# Final output for structured reporting
results_json <- list(
  metric = "sample_size",
  value = min_n,
  unit = "participants_per_group",
  method = "two_sample_t",
  design_parameters = list(

    effect_size_cohens_d = round(cohens_d, 4)
  ),
  power_verification = list(
    power_at_minimum = round(power_calc(min_n), 4),
    power_at_preceding = if (min_n > 1) round(power_calc(min_n - 1), 4) else NA
  )
)

cat("\n")
POWER_AGENT_RESULT=jsonlite::toJSON(list(results = list(
  list(metric = "sample_size", value = min_n, unit = "participants_per_group")
)), auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15)

# Two-sample t-test sample size calculation
# Design: one-sided test, H0: μ_t = μ_c vs H1: μ_t > μ_c
# Parameters
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.80
delta <- 4.3  # expected difference (dBA)
sigma <- 7.8  # common SD (dBA)
allocation_ratio <- 1  # 1:1 allocation

# Critical value for one-sided test
z_alpha <- qnorm(1 - alpha)

# Non-centrality parameter coefficient
# For two-sample t-test with equal allocation: ncp = delta / (sigma * sqrt(2/n))
# Effect size (Cohen's d)
cohens_d <- delta / sigma
cat("Cohen's d (effect size):", round(cohens_d, 4), "\n")
cat("Z-critical (one-sided, alpha=0.05):", round(z_alpha, 4), "\n\n")

# Search for minimum n per group
# Start with a reasonable guess based on normal approximation
n_approx <- 2 * ((z_alpha + qnorm(target_power)) / cohens_d)^2
cat("Approximate n per group (normal approximation):", round(n_approx, 1), "\n\n")

# Refine with t-distribution
# For one-sided test: df = 2n - 2, critical value = t_{1-alpha, df}
# Non-centrality parameter: lambda = (delta / sigma) * sqrt(n/2)
# Power = P(T > t_{1-alpha, df} | lambda)

# Function to calculate power given n per group
power_calc <- function(n_per_group) {
  if (n_per_group < 1) return(0)
  
  df <- 2 * n_per_group - 2
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df)  # Critical value for one-sided test
  
  # Non-centrality parameter
  # lambda = (difference / sigma) * sqrt(n / 2) for equal sample sizes
  lambda <- (delta / sigma) * sqrt(n_per_group / 2)
  
  # Power: probability that non-central t > critical value
  power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp = lambda)
  
  return(power)
}

# Search for minimum integer n
powers <- numeric(100)
ns <- 1:100

for (i in 1:100) {
  powers[i] <- power_calc(i)
}

# Find minimum n achieving target power
min_n <- which(powers >= target_power)[1]

cat("Sample size search results:\n")
cat("n per group | Power\n")
cat("------------|-------\n")

# Show values around minimum
for (n_test in max(1, min_n - 2):min(min_n + 2, 100)) {
  p <- power_calc(n_test)
  marker <- if (n_test == min_n) " <-- MINIMUM" else ""
  cat(sprintf("%11d | %6.4f%s\n", n_test, p, marker))
}

cat("\n=== RESULT ===\n")
cat("Minimum sample size per group achieving ≥80% power:", min_n, "\n")
cat("Power at minimum n =", min_n, ":", round(power_calc(min_n), 4), "\n")

if (min_n > 1) {

}
